open_obligations: Review the full Saxe assumptions and test any proposed transfer to the fine-tuning system.
in.rationale: Betley et al. use “training dynamics” in their §4.7 heading “Training dynamics of emergent misalignment”, in a study of narrow LLM fine-tuning; Saxe et al. study “dynamics of learning” in restricted deep linear networks. Both discuss how models change over training, but neither bears on the other's claim: this is a terminology-based research lead, not an explanation of LLM behavior by the deep-linear model.
in.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: training dynamics in LLM fine-tuning (Betley et al. §4.7) and learning dynamics in restricted deep linear networks (Saxe et al.); cross-paper wording for navigation only

text: The pinned abstract reports an analysis of restricted deep linear networks whose gradient-descent weight dynamics are nonlinear despite a linear input-output map, with long plateaus, rapid transitions, and initialization-dependent learning speed. The abstract alone does not license transfer to modern LLM fine-tuning.
title: Saxe et al.: deep-linear learning trajectories
